ics.description: Look {{from}} at {{time}}. It climbs {{height}} and sets {{to}}. {{brightness}}, visible for about {{minutes}} min. A steady moving light, no blinking. From KeepTrack Visible Tonight.

VisibleTonight.privacyNote: Your location stays in this browser tab and is not saved or sent anywhere. Brightness is an estimate.

help.overview: Visible Tonight lists the bright satellites, like the International Space Station, that you can see from where you are over the next few nights, with no telescope or settings needed.
help.howToUse:
1. Open Visible Tonight and tap Use my location.
  2. Pick a pass: it tells you when, where it rises and sets, and how bright it is.
  3. Tap Add to calendar to get a reminder.
  4. Tap the pass itself to watch it in KeepTrack.
help.tip1: Satellites are easiest to see shortly after sunset or before sunrise, when your sky is dark but they are still in sunlight.
help.tip2: Need more control, like other sensors or every pass? Try Best Passes or Look Angles.
